html:
Melegueta pepper, or grains of paradise, a spice from a West African plant that Portuguese sailors bought on the coast of today's Liberia from the 1460s, which they named the Grain Coast after it.

Europeans had bought it earlier through the Saharan trade as a cheaper stand-in for black pepper, and buying it at the source was one of the first gains of the Portuguese voyages. When Asian pepper came in by sea after 1500, the trade shrank. The coast had no great harbour or kingdom, so it saw fewer forts than the Gold Coast, but its Kru seamen later worked on European ships. See also Portuguese exploration.
sum: Melegueta pepper, or grains of paradise, a spice from a West African plant that Portuguese sailors bought on the coast of today's Liberia from the 1460s, which they named the Grain Coast after it.
